# Turtle { #turtle_widget.Turtle }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle(
    width=500,
    height=500,
    show_code=False,
    code=None,
    autoshow=True,
    bg='white',
    home=None,
)
```

An animated, turtle-compatible drawing widget for Jupyter notebooks.

Turtle commands are recorded in Python as a stream of events and replayed as a
canvas animation below the cell. The widget displays itself automatically at the
end of the cell; you can also call ``show()`` or evaluate the turtle to display it.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**width**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [500]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Canvas width in pixels. Default 500.

<code>[**height**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [500]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Canvas height in pixels. Default 500.

<code>[**show_code**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True, show the cell source beside the canvas and highlight the active line in sync with the animation. Default False.

<code>[**code**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Source to display instead of the captured cell source.

<code>[**autoshow**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True (default), display the widget automatically at the end of the cell. Set False for headless use such as tests.

<code>[**bg**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'white\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Canvas background colour. Default ``"white"``.

<code>[**home**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of float]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   The turtle's home, given as ``(x, y)`` or ``(x, y, heading)`` (heading defaults to 0; 0 = east). Defaults to the origin ``(0, 0)`` facing east. The turtle both **starts** here and returns here on :func:`home`. (To re-target the home of an existing turtle *without* moving it, call :func:`sethome`.)

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

<code>[**nr_collisions**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Running count of collisions detected since the turtle was created (reset to 0 by :func:`reset`). Incremented once per collision reported while an :func:`on_collision` handler is active — so with the default ``stop=True`` it counts the obstacles the turtle has run into, and with ``stop=False`` every crossing reported. Starts at 0.

<code>[**nr_left, nr_right**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Number of times :func:`left` / :func:`right` has been called. Starts at 0, reset by :func:`reset`. (The aliases ``lt``/``rt`` count too, as they are the same methods.)

<code>[**nr_sense, nr_distance_ahead**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Number of times :func:`sense` / :func:`distance_ahead` has been called. Starts at 0, reset by :func:`reset`. ``nearest`` is not counted (it does not call ``sense``).

<code>[**total_movement**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Total distance the turtle has travelled, in turtle units, summed over every move (``forward``/``backward``/``goto``/``circle``/``home``/…), whether the pen is up or down. A move stopped short by a collision contributes only the distance actually travelled; turns contribute nothing. Starts at 0.0, reset by :func:`reset`.

| [add_circle](#turtle_widget.Turtle.add_circle) | Register a circular obstacle and draw it. |
| [add_polygon](#turtle_widget.Turtle.add_polygon) | Register a filled polygon obstacle and draw it. |
| [add_rectangle](#turtle_widget.Turtle.add_rectangle) | Register a rectangular obstacle (a 4-point polygon) and draw it. |
| [add_segment](#turtle_widget.Turtle.add_segment) | Register a line-segment (wall) obstacle and draw it. |
| [backward](#turtle_widget.Turtle.backward) | Move the turtle backward by ``distance`` (opposite its heading). |
| [begin_fill](#turtle_widget.Turtle.begin_fill) | Start recording a filled shape. |
| [bgcolor](#turtle_widget.Turtle.bgcolor) | Get or set the canvas background colour. |
| [circle](#turtle_widget.Turtle.circle) | Draw a circle or arc, approximated by a series of straight chords. |
| [clear](#turtle_widget.Turtle.clear) | Clear the drawing and the sensed trail from the canvas. |
| [color](#turtle_widget.Turtle.color) | Get or set the pen colour, the fill colour, or both at once. |
| [distance_ahead](#turtle_widget.Turtle.distance_ahead) | Sense the nearest obstacle straight ahead. |
| [dot](#turtle_widget.Turtle.dot) | Draw a filled dot at the current position. |
| [duration](#turtle_widget.Turtle.duration) | Total time the animation will take to play, in seconds. |
| [end_fill](#turtle_widget.Turtle.end_fill) | Fill the shape traced since the last ``begin_fill``. |
| [fillcolor](#turtle_widget.Turtle.fillcolor) | Get or set the fill colour used by ``begin_fill`` / ``end_fill``. |
| [forward](#turtle_widget.Turtle.forward) | Move the turtle forward by ``distance``, drawing if the pen is down. |
| [goto](#turtle_widget.Turtle.goto) | Move the turtle to an absolute position, drawing if the pen is down. |
| [heading](#turtle_widget.Turtle.heading) | Return the current heading in degrees. |
| [hide_obstacles](#turtle_widget.Turtle.hide_obstacles) | Hide all registered obstacles from view. |
| [hideturtle](#turtle_widget.Turtle.hideturtle) | Hide the turtle marker. |
| [home](#turtle_widget.Turtle.home) | Move the turtle to its home position and turn to the home heading. |
| [isdown](#turtle_widget.Turtle.isdown) | Return whether the pen is down. |
| [isvisible](#turtle_widget.Turtle.isvisible) | Return whether the turtle marker is visible. |
| [left](#turtle_widget.Turtle.left) | Turn the turtle counter-clockwise by ``angle`` degrees. |
| [nearest](#turtle_widget.Turtle.nearest) | The single nearest obstacle within range, or ``None``. |
| [on_collision](#turtle_widget.Turtle.on_collision) | Register a hook fired when a move runs into an obstacle. |
| [pencolor](#turtle_widget.Turtle.pencolor) | Get or set the pen (outline) colour. |
| [pendown](#turtle_widget.Turtle.pendown) | Lower the pen so subsequent moves draw. |
| [pensize](#turtle_widget.Turtle.pensize) | Get or set the pen width. |
| [penup](#turtle_widget.Turtle.penup) | Lift the pen so subsequent moves do not draw. |
| [position](#turtle_widget.Turtle.position) | Return the current position. |
| [reset](#turtle_widget.Turtle.reset) | Clear the drawing and reset the turtle to its initial state. |
| [right](#turtle_widget.Turtle.right) | Turn the turtle clockwise by ``angle`` degrees. |
| [sense](#turtle_widget.Turtle.sense) | Detect all obstacles within range, with the bearing to each. |
| [setheading](#turtle_widget.Turtle.setheading) | Turn the turtle to face an absolute heading. |
| [sethome](#turtle_widget.Turtle.sethome) | Set the home position that :func:`home` returns to. |
| [setx](#turtle_widget.Turtle.setx) | Set the x-coordinate, keeping y unchanged. |
| [sety](#turtle_widget.Turtle.sety) | Set the y-coordinate, keeping x unchanged. |
| [show](#turtle_widget.Turtle.show) | Flush the recorded commands and display the widget now. |
| [show_obstacles](#turtle_widget.Turtle.show_obstacles) | Make all registered obstacles visible. |
| [showturtle](#turtle_widget.Turtle.showturtle) | Make the turtle marker visible. |
| [speed](#turtle_widget.Turtle.speed) | Get or set the drawing speed. |
| [stamp](#turtle_widget.Turtle.stamp) | Stamp a copy of the turtle shape at the current position and heading. |
| [write](#turtle_widget.Turtle.write) | Write text at the current position. |
| [xcor](#turtle_widget.Turtle.xcor) | Return the current x-coordinate. |
| [ycor](#turtle_widget.Turtle.ycor) | Return the current y-coordinate. |

### add_circle { #turtle_widget.Turtle.add_circle }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle.add_circle(
    x,
    y,
    radius,
    color=None,
    visible=True,
    label=None,
    sense=True,
)
```

Register a circular obstacle and draw it.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**x**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Centre of the circle, in turtle coordinates.

<code>[**y**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Centre of the circle, in turtle coordinates.

<code>[**radius**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Radius of the circle.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) or [tuple](`tuple`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Outline/fill colour. Defaults to a neutral obstacle colour.

<code>[**visible**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Whether to draw it (default True). Invisible obstacles are still sensed and still collide.

<code>[**label**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   A name carried on the obstacle and surfaced as ``.label`` on the ``Detection``/``Collision`` objects that report it. Not drawn.

<code>[**sense**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Whether ``distance_ahead``/``sense``/``nearest`` can detect it (default True). A non-sensing obstacle is still drawn (unless ``visible=False``) and still collides — it is only hidden from the sensing queries.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Turtle](`turtle_widget.widget.Turtle`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   This turtle, to allow method chaining.

### circle { #turtle_widget.Turtle.circle }

```python

Draw a circle or arc, approximated by a series of straight chords.

A positive ``radius`` curves to the left of the turtle, a negative ``radius``
to the right.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**radius**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Radius of the circle. Positive curves left, negative curves right.

:   Angle of the arc to draw, in degrees. Defaults to 360 (a full circle).

<code>[**steps**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[int](`int`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Number of chords approximating the arc. Defaults to a value scaled to the radius and extent.

<code>[**speed**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [1.0]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Per-move multiplier on the global ``speed()`` (2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half). Default 1.0.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Turtle](`turtle_widget.widget.Turtle`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   This turtle, to allow method chaining.

```

### distance_ahead { #turtle_widget.Turtle.distance_ahead }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle.distance_ahead(
    max_distance=None,
    walls=True,
    trail=True,
    draw=False,
    color='red',
)
```

Sense the nearest obstacle straight ahead.

Casts a ray from the turtle along its current heading and returns the first
obstacle it hits as a ``Detection`` — the same object :func:`sense` yields.
Increments ``nr_distance_ahead``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**max_distance**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Ignore hits farther than this. ``None`` (default) means unlimited.

<code>[**walls**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Include the canvas border as an obstacle. Default True.

<code>[**trail**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Include the turtle's own drawn path as obstacles. Default True.

<code>[**draw**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True, also draw the sensor ray on the canvas. Default False.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) or [tuple](`tuple`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'red\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Colour of the drawn ray, used only when ``draw=True``. Default ``"red"``; accepts a CSS colour string or an ``(r, g, b)`` tuple.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Detection](`turtle_widget.widget.Detection`) or None]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The nearest obstacle ahead, with the same fields as a ``sense`` result — ``distance``, ``angle`` (the signed angle of incidence — 0 = head-on, ±90 = grazing), ``point``, ``obstacle`` (the shape hit), ``kind`` and ``index`` — or ``None`` if nothing is within range.

### duration { #turtle_widget.Turtle.duration }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle.duration()
```

Total time the animation will take to play, in seconds.

Computed from the recorded events using the exact timing the browser uses: a
``line``/``move`` of length *d* at effective speed *s* takes ``d / (s * 150)``
seconds, a ``turn`` of *a* degrees takes ``a / (s * 180)`` seconds, and every
other event (dots, stamps, writes, fills, pen/colour changes, sensing, …) is
instant. A move whose effective speed is ``0`` is instant too — it snaps into
place. The effective speed already includes any per-move ``speed=`` multiplier.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Seconds the full animation will take at the current events' speeds. ``0.0`` if speed is ``0`` (everything is instant) or nothing has been drawn yet.

#### Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

This is the *scheduled* play time derived from the event stream — it excludes the
browser's frame-scheduling overhead and does not change as the animation plays.
The *currently elapsed* time lives in the browser; the Python ``Turtle`` records
events but does not receive playback progress back, so live elapsed/remaining time
is not readable here. (It could be exposed by adding a synced trait the frontend
updates each frame — ask if you want that.)

### on_collision { #turtle_widget.Turtle.on_collision }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle.on_collision(handler, stop=True, walls=True, trail=False)
```

Register a hook fired when a move runs into an obstacle.

Collision detection is **opt-in** — calling this enables it; until then moves are
unaffected. By default the turtle **stops at the first obstacle (or canvas edge) it
hits**: the move is shortened to the contact point and the turtle ends there. After a
move that hit something, ``handler(collision)`` is called with the contact details;
the handler may then issue ordinary turtle commands (which animate next) to react.
Each reported collision also increments the turtle's ``nr_collisions`` counter.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**handler**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[callable](`callable`) or None]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Called as ``handler(collision)`` with a ``Collision`` (see Notes). Pass ``None`` to turn collision detection off again.

<code>[**stop**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True (default), the turtle stops at the first contact. If False, motion is unchanged (the move completes) and the handler is notified for *every* obstacle the path crossed, nearest first.

<code>[**walls**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Treat the canvas border as an obstacle. Default True.

<code>[**trail**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Also collide with the turtle's own drawn path (self-collision). Default False.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Turtle](`turtle_widget.widget.Turtle`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   This turtle, to allow method chaining.

#### Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

Each ``Collision`` carries the contact ``point`` (x, y); the ``obstacle`` that was hit
(an ``Obstacle`` exposing ``.kind`` —
``"circle"``/``"segment"``/``"polygon"``/``"wall"``/``"trail"`` — plus ``.label`` and its
geometry); its ``index`` among registered obstacles (else ``None``); the unit surface
``normal`` at the contact,
facing back toward the turtle (reflect a direction ``d`` with ``d - 2*(d·n)*n`` to
bounce); the ``distance`` travelled into the move; ``angle``, the signed angle of
incidence in degrees (0 = a head-on, perpendicular hit; ±90 = a grazing hit parallel to
the surface; the sign distinguishes the two glancing sides); ``speed``, the effective
animation speed of the move (global ``speed()`` × the move's ``speed=`` multiplier);
and the turtle's state — ``pos``, ``heading``, ``isdown``, ``isvisible``, ``pencolor``,
``pensize``. The handler's own moves do not re-trigger collisions, so it can move the
turtle freely (e.g. to bounce or back away).

### sense { #turtle_widget.Turtle.sense }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle.sense(
    max_distance=None,
    walls=True,
    trail=True,
    draw=False,
    color='red',
)
```

Detect all obstacles within range, with the bearing to each.

For every obstacle whose closest point lies within ``max_distance`` of
the turtle, returns a ``Detection`` giving the distance and the signed
angle (relative to the turtle's heading, positive = left / counter-
clockwise) to that closest point. A point the turtle is touching is not
reported. Increments ``nr_sense`` (``nearest`` does not, since it does not
call this method).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**max_distance**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Only report obstacles whose closest point is within this distance. ``None`` (default) reports every obstacle.

<code>[**walls**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Include the canvas border. Default True.

<code>[**trail**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Include the turtle's own drawn path (its nearest point). Default True.

<code>[**draw**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [False]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If True, also draw a ray to each detected point. Default False.

<code>[**color**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`) or [tuple](`tuple`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'red\']{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Colour of the drawn rays, used only when ``draw=True``. Default ``"red"``; accepts a CSS colour string or an ``(r, g, b)`` tuple.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [list of Detection]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Detections sorted nearest-first. Each ``Detection`` has fields ``distance``, ``angle`` (degrees), ``point`` (x, y), ``obstacle`` (the shape hit — an ``Obstacle`` exposing ``.kind``/``.label``/geometry), ``kind`` (one of ``"circle"``, ``"segment"``, ``"polygon"``, ``"wall"``, ``"trail"``) and ``index`` (position among registered obstacles, else ``None``).

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**text**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The text to write.

<code>[**align**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(\'left\', \'center\', \'right\')]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\"left\"]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Horizontal alignment relative to the turtle. Default ``"left"``.

<code>[**font**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[tuple](`tuple`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [(\'sans-serif\', 14, \'normal\')]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   A ``(family, size, style)`` triple; only family and size are used. Default ``("sans-serif", 14, "normal")``.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Turtle](`turtle_widget.widget.Turtle`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   This turtle, to allow method chaining.

### xcor { #turtle_widget.Turtle.xcor }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle.xcor()
```

Return the current x-coordinate.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The current x-coordinate.

### ycor { #turtle_widget.Turtle.ycor }

```python
turtle_widget.Turtle.ycor()
```

Return the current y-coordinate.

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The current y-coordinate.
